title: PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) Carried-In Credit: Reserve Daily Cost by Billing History
content:
For the cut-over reserve kept back from a credit balance carried into PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering), the reserve daily cost is set by the standard billing history of the enrolled service account, read from its Electric Service by Rate Schedule records: the standard bills, their usage lines and the kWh on their energy lines.

**Rule.** Where the enrolled service account carries at least 12 standard bills in the twelve-month window and the energy line of its most recent bill carries fewer kWh than the average energy line of the bills in that window, the reserve daily cost is the total of the usage lines in the twelve-month window divided by 365. Where it carries at least 6 but fewer than 12 standard bills in the twelve-month window, the reserve daily cost is the total of the usage lines in the six-month window divided by 182. An account in any other situation keeps the most recent bill's daily cost.

**Windows.** A window of a stated number of months takes the records dated after the same day of the month that many months before the current date, through the current date.

### Decision table

| Standard bills in the twelve-month window | Most recent energy line below the window's average energy line | Reserve daily cost |
|---|---|---|
| 12 or more | yes | usage lines of the twelve-month window divided by 365 |
| 12 or more | no | keeps the most recent bill's daily cost |
| 6 to 11 | either | usage lines of the six-month window divided by 182 |
| 5 or fewer | either | keeps the most recent bill's daily cost |

The average energy line is the total kWh of the energy lines in the twelve-month window divided by the number of bills in it.

### Hypothetical histories

- 12 bills, usage lines totalling 1460.00 in the twelve-month window, energy lines averaging 900 kWh, most recent energy line 610 kWh: 610 is below 900, so the reserve daily cost is 1460.00 divided by 365, which is 4.00.
- 11 bills, with usage lines of 455.00 in the six-month window: 11 is at least 6 and fewer than 12, so the reserve daily cost is 455.00 divided by 182, which is 2.50.
- 12 bills but a most recent energy line of 950 kWh against an average of 900 kWh: not below the average, so the account keeps the most recent bill's daily cost.
